changes.after: An RDS file stores an R object so it can be read back with its structure intact. Use a file you trust.

before: saveRDS writes one R object, preserving R-specific structure such as classes and attributes; readRDS returns the object instead of choosing a variable name in the caller. Assign its result explicitly. This differs from a plain-text CSV interchange.

The fixture writes and reads its own local object. RDS is not a safe interchange boundary for arbitrary untrusted files and is not guaranteed portable forever across versions or systems. Validate the loaded shape and record provenance; do not execute unknown serialized content as a substitute for a documented data format.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
entry <- list(topic = "read", minutes = 15)
saveRDS(entry, "entry.rds")
restored <- readRDS("entry.rds")
cat(identical(entry, restored), "\n", sep = "")
cat(restored$minutes, "\n", sep = "")

```

Expected output or behavior: TRUE
15. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
